5f26fbd0.text: Welcome to the Midnight Tribunal. Tonight you did something a little decadent, and now your conscience has hired lawyers. Three real philosophers are about to put you on trial. Whenever it's your turn to answer, I'll stop and wait for you.
5f26fbd0.spoken: Welcome to the Midnight Tribunal. Tonight you did something a little decadent, and now your conscience has hired lawyers. Three real philosophers are about to put you on trial. Whenever it's your turn to answer, I'll stop and wait for you.

f875b852.text: First, the evidence. This afternoon, on a whim, you bought a forty-dollar slice of chocolate cake, covered in gold leaf.
f875b852.spoken: First, the evidence. This afternoon, on a whim, you bought a forty-dollar slice of chocolate cake, covered in gold leaf.

8f10ea6e.text: You ate the whole thing yourself, in about four minutes.
8f10ea6e.spoken: You ate the whole thing yourself, in about four minutes.

4351195b.text: Three friends were sitting right there. You didn't offer them a single bite.
4351195b.spoken: Three friends were sitting right there. You didn't offer them a single bite.

4fc93b9d.text: By the tenth bite you felt a little sick. By bedtime you were queasy, and oddly guilty.
4fc93b9d.spoken: By the tenth bite you felt a little sick. By bedtime you were queasy, and oddly guilty.

913073d3.text: Now you're asleep. And the dream is strange.
913073d3.spoken: Now you're asleep. And the dream is strange.

368388a1.text: You're standing in a foggy courtroom. A giant set of scales hangs overhead. Three robed figures step forward, and they want to settle one question. Did that cake actually make your life better? Each judge is a real philosopher. Together they trace the road to utilitarianism: the view that what's good is well-being, and that the right act is the one that produces the most of it.
368388a1.spoken: You're standing in a foggy courtroom. A giant set of scales hangs overhead. Three robed figures step forward, and they want to settle one question. Did that cake actually make your life better? Each judge is a real philosopher. Together they trace the road to utilitarianism: the view that what's good is well-being, and that the right act is the one that produces the most of it.

1e161894.text: Before the judges speak, tell them where you stand. Rate each of these five statements. There are no right answers here, so just be honest, and press Submit when you're done.
1e161894.spoken: Before the judges speak, tell them where you stand. Rate each of these five statements. There are no right answers here, so just be honest, and press Submit when you're done.

a5742dd8.text: Saved. You'll come back to these at the end, once all three judges have spoken.
a5742dd8.spoken: Saved. You'll come back to these at the end, once all three judges have spoken.

3bb67ffd.text: The first judge is Epicurus, a Greek philosopher who taught in a garden in Athens more than two thousand years ago. He hasn't come to scold pleasure, he tells you. He worships it. Epicurus is a hedonist. He holds that pleasure is the only thing good in itself, and pain the only thing bad in itself. Money, fame, even cake: these are good only when they bring pleasure or keep pain away.
3bb67ffd.spoken: The first judge is Epicurus, a Greek philosopher who taught in a garden in Athens more than two thousand years ago. He hasn't come to scold pleasure, he tells you. He worships it. Epicurus is a hedonist. He holds that pleasure is the only thing good in itself, and pain the only thing bad in itself. Money, fame, even cake: these are good only when they bring pleasure or keep pain away.

34545d6c.text: So why does Epicurus frown at your cake? Because he sorts desires into three bins.
34545d6c.spoken: So why does Epicurus frown at your cake? Because he sorts desires into three bins.

e06cb480.text: First, desires that are natural and necessary: food when you're hungry, shelter, friends, understanding. They're easy to satisfy, and going without them really hurts.
e06cb480.spoken: First, desires that are natural and necessary: food when you're hungry, shelter, friends, understanding. They're easy to satisfy, and going without them really hurts.

3df4a6ea.text: Second, desires that are natural but unnecessary. You need food, but you don't need gold leaf on it. Pleasant, yes, but they scratch an itch you never needed to have.
3df4a6ea.spoken: Second, desires that are natural but unnecessary. You need food, but you don't need gold leaf on it. Pleasant, yes, but they scratch an itch you never needed to have.

3a01834a.text: Third, desires that are vain and empty: fame, status, the most expensive thing on the menu. These can never be fully satisfied, Epicurus warns, so they breed anxiety.
3a01834a.spoken: Third, desires that are vain and empty: fame, status, the most expensive thing on the menu. These can never be fully satisfied, Epicurus warns, so they breed anxiety.

a691ab85.text: For Epicurus, the aim of life isn't intense pleasure. It's ataraxia: a calm, steady contentment, free from fear and pain.
a691ab85.spoken: For Epicurus, the aim of life isn't intense pleasure. It's ataraxia: a calm, steady contentment, free from fear and pain.

547907fe.text: Intense, fleeting thrills often cost more than they pay. Your cake bought four minutes of bliss, then a night of nausea and guilt. By Epicurus's reckoning, that's a net loss.
547907fe.spoken: Intense, fleeting thrills often cost more than they pay. Your cake bought four minutes of bliss, then a night of nausea and guilt. By Epicurus's reckoning, that's a net loss.

0e17d25a.text: His greatest source of happiness is friendship. Of everything wisdom provides for a happy life, he wrote, friendship is by far the greatest.
0e17d25a.spoken: His greatest source of happiness is friendship. Of everything wisdom provides for a happy life, he wrote, friendship is by far the greatest.

c2e71209.text: Yet you ate alone, with three friends sitting right there. You traded the deepest pleasure for a sugar rush.
c2e71209.spoken: Yet you ate alone, with three friends sitting right there. You traded the deepest pleasure for a sugar rush.

4ab7ca9f.text: Epicurus wants to see whether you were listening. Put each desire in one of his three bins, then press Check answers.
4ab7ca9f.spoken: Epicurus wants to see whether you were listening. Put each desire in one of his three bins, then press Check answers.

4ac95d51.text: Now say it back. Fill in the blanks to complete Epicurus's verdict, then press Check.
4ac95d51.spoken: Now say it back. Fill in the blanks to complete Epicurus's verdict, then press Check.

0bf7af6a.text: Both views on screen are hedonist, so they agree that pleasure is the good. They split on one question: whose pleasure do you have to weigh? The egoistic hedonist says only your own. Eat all twelve bites, and your friends' hunger isn't your concern. The hedonistic utilitarian says everyone's pleasure counts equally, so you share the cake to make the total as large as possible. This afternoon, you acted like an egoist. The next judge insists that everyone counts.
0bf7af6a.spoken: Both views on screen are hedonist, so they agree that pleasure is the good. They split on one question: whose pleasure do you have to weigh? The egoistic hedonist says only your own. Eat all twelve bites, and your friends' hunger isn't your concern. The hedonistic utilitarian says everyone's pleasure counts equally, so you share the cake to make the total as large as possible. This afternoon, you acted like an egoist. The next judge insists that everyone counts.

5658251f.text: The second judge is Jeremy Bentham, an English philosopher and reformer who lived from 1748 to 1832. He's holding a ledger, and he says you forgot to do the math. Bentham turned hedonism into a public rule, which he called the principle of utility. The right action is the one that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number. And in that sum, everyone counts equally. Each person counts for one, and no one for more than one.
5658251f.spoken: The second judge is Jeremy Bentham, an English philosopher and reformer who lived from 1748 to 1832. He's holding a ledger, and he says you forgot to do the math. Bentham turned hedonism into a public rule, which he called the principle of utility. The right action is the one that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number. And in that sum, everyone counts equally. Each person counts for one, and no one for more than one.

a0d63ad8.text: Bentham thought you could actually weigh a pleasure. His hedonic calculus scores it along seven dimensions, and only these seven.
a0d63ad8.spoken: Bentham thought you could actually weigh a pleasure. His hedonic calculus scores it along seven dimensions, and only these seven.

49420a75.text: Intensity: how strong is it? And duration: how long does it last?
49420a75.spoken: Intensity: how strong is it? And duration: how long does it last?

a6b2389f.text: Certainty: how likely is it to happen? And propinquity: how soon will it come?
a6b2389f.spoken: Certainty: how likely is it to happen? And propinquity: how soon will it come?

f47f272e.text: Fecundity: will it lead to more pleasure later? And purity: will it steer clear of pain later?
f47f272e.spoken: Fecundity: will it lead to more pleasure later? And purity: will it steer clear of pain later?

6819462d.text: And finally, extent, the crucial one. How many people does it reach?
6819462d.spoken: And finally, extent, the crucial one. How many people does it reach?

23286107.text: Two ideas convict you, says Bentham.
23286107.spoken: Two ideas convict you, says Bentham.

88552df8.text: The first is extent. One happy person adds up to far less happiness than four happy people. Split four ways, the same cake does more good in the world.
88552df8.spoken: The first is extent. One happy person adds up to far less happiness than four happy people. Split four ways, the same cake does more good in the world.

4ddacdee.text: The second is diminishing returns. Your first bite was ecstasy. Your tenth made you queasy. Each extra bite gave you less pleasure than the one before.
4ddacdee.spoken: The second is diminishing returns. Your first bite was ecstasy. Your tenth made you queasy. Each extra bite gave you less pleasure than the one before.

606e9b2f.text: So a bite handed to a friend who's had none adds more happiness than the same bite piled onto you, already stuffed.
606e9b2f.spoken: So a bite handed to a friend who's had none adds more happiness than the same bite piled onto you, already stuffed.

7df4f046.text: The verdict: sharing wasn't just nice. It was the option that produced the most total happiness.
7df4f046.spoken: The verdict: sharing wasn't just nice. It was the option that produced the most total happiness.

a48e5bfd.text: Now try it yourself. Bentham hands you the cake. Use the minus and plus buttons to move bites between you, Ana, Ben, and Cy, and watch each person's happiness and the total. Notice how the next bite is worth less as someone eats more. When you've found the best split, press Continue.
a48e5bfd.spoken: Now try it yourself. Bentham hands you the cake. Use the minus and plus buttons to move bites between you, Ana, Ben, and Sigh, and watch each person's happiness and the total. Notice how the next bite is worth less as someone eats more. When you've found the best split, press Continue.

478f3927.text: Bentham wants to check your arithmetic. Mark every factor that belongs in his hedonic calculus, then press Check answers.
478f3927.spoken: Bentham wants to check your arithmetic. Mark every factor that belongs in his hedonic calculus, then press Check answers.

be0617c0.text: One more from Bentham. On his principle, why would sharing the cake have been the better act? Pick the best answer.
be0617c0.spoken: One more from Bentham. On his principle, why would sharing the cake have been the better act? Pick the best answer.

36fecbc2.text: Here's a split inside utilitarianism itself. Two utilitarians can agree completely that we should maximize happiness, and still disagree about what to judge. The act utilitarian judges each action by its own consequences, case by case. On that view, if a selfish exception really does win the sum, you should take it. The rule utilitarian follows the rules that would produce the most happiness if people generally kept them. So the rule utilitarian keeps a rule like sharing treats with friends, even when an exception tempts you.

The rule utilitarian follows the rules that would produce the most happiness if people generally kept them. So the rule utilitarian keeps a rule like sharing treats with friends, even when an exception tempts you.

3891e089.text: Your turn to decide, and this one isn't graded. Suppose you could eat the whole cake and nobody would ever know. Which question should you be asking? Pick the answer closest to your own view, then read the note that comes with it.

b31d06cb.text: Before the third judge speaks, someone in the gallery raises a hand. It's John Stuart Mill, who grew up in Bentham's circle, and he has a quick objection about the quality of your pleasure. Mill worried that Bentham's math treats every pleasure as the same kind of stuff. He disagreed. Some pleasures, he argued, are higher in quality than others.
b31d06cb.spoken: Before the third judge speaks, someone in the gallery raises a hand. It's John Stuart Mill, who grew up in Bentham's circle, and he has a quick objection about the quality of your pleasure. Mill worried that Bentham's math treats every pleasure as the same kind of stuff. He disagreed. Some pleasures, he argued, are higher in quality than others.

b265a8b0.text: Your cake is a lower pleasure, a bodily one. Fine, but shallow.
b265a8b0.spoken: Your cake is a lower pleasure, a bodily one. Fine, but shallow.

6ebf3e11.text: Conversation, art, and learning are higher pleasures. For Mill, they're worth more, even in smaller amounts.
6ebf3e11.spoken: Conversation, art, and learning are higher pleasures. For Mill, they're worth more, even in smaller amounts.

6734a46b.text: As he famously put it, it's better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
6734a46b.spoken: As he famously put it, it's better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.

a421a127.text: The third judge is Peter Singer, an Australian philosopher of our own time, and he wants to widen the circle. Your friends, he says, aren't the only ones with a stake in that cake. For most of his career, Singer was a preference utilitarian: what matters is satisfying the preferences of everyone affected. In 2014 he came round to hedonism. Either way, he insists on equal consideration for every being that can suffer, human or not.
a421a127.spoken: The third judge is Peter Singer, an Australian philosopher of our own time, and he wants to widen the circle. Your friends, he says, aren't the only ones with a stake in that cake. For most of his career, Singer was a preference utilitarian: what matters is satisfying the preferences of everyone affected. In 2014 he came round to hedonism. Either way, he insists on equal consideration for every being that can suffer, human or not.

aa191883.text: Preference utilitarians, as Singer long was, part ways with Bentham over what well-being even is. For the hedonist, the only good is pleasure and the absence of pain, so the cake is good simply because it tastes wonderful. For the preference utilitarian, the good is satisfying the preferences that beings actually have. Your friends wanted a bite of that cake. On this view, their preference counts, even if missing out never caused them a moment's pain.

11e25e79.text: Singer's first lesson is about what you eat. He points at the cream and the eggs in your cake. Ignoring an animal's suffering just because it isn't human, he argues, is speciesism: a bias as arbitrary as racism.
11e25e79.spoken: Singer's first lesson is about what you eat. He points at the cream and the eggs in your cake. Ignoring an animal's suffering just because it isn't human, he argues, is speciesism: a bias as arbitrary as racism.

c6ebc94d.text: The animals behind factory-farmed dairy and eggs have a real interest in not suffering.
c6ebc94d.spoken: The animals behind factory-farmed dairy and eggs have a real interest in not suffering.

7e83d225.text: That interest counts in the moral sum. It doesn't vanish just because they can't argue their case in court.
7e83d225.spoken: That interest counts in the moral sum. It doesn't vanish just because they can't argue their case in court.

0704adb8.text: So Singer's verdict on what to eat: lean toward foods that cause far less suffering, which mostly means plant-based ones.
0704adb8.spoken: So Singer's verdict on what to eat: lean toward foods that cause far less suffering, which mostly means plant-based ones.

2b560c11.text: His second lesson is about the price tag, and it comes with his most famous thought experiment.
2b560c11.spoken: His second lesson is about the price tag, and it comes with his most famous thought experiment.

ace17085.text: Imagine you could save a child drowning in a shallow pond, but it would ruin your forty-dollar shoes. Obviously you should save the child. And for Singer, distance and strangers don't change the math.
ace17085.spoken: Imagine you could save a child drowning in a shallow pond, but it would ruin your forty-dollar shoes. Obviously you should save the child. And for Singer, distance and strangers don't change the math.

4e15f19a.text: Right now, forty dollars given to a highly effective charity can protect real children from deadly disease.
4e15f19a.spoken: Right now, forty dollars given to a highly effective charity can protect real children from deadly disease.

6554e129.text: Your cake bought four minutes of solo pleasure. The same money could have prevented serious suffering. That idea sits at the heart of effective altruism.
6554e129.spoken: Your cake bought four minutes of solo pleasure. The same money could have prevented serious suffering. That idea sits at the heart of effective altruism.

bca65f11.text: Singer's forty dollars raises a worry. Must we always do the very most good we can? Utilitarians answer in two ways. Maximizers say yes. You're obligated to produce the greatest good possible, so buying a forty-dollar cake is wrong, and that money should have gone wherever it would do the most good. It's a very demanding view. Satisficers say you only have to produce enough good, clearing a reasonable threshold. An occasional treat is fine, as long as you're already doing your fair share.

128cae24.text: Another decision, and again it isn't graded. Singer says that forty dollars should have gone where it would do the most good. How much does morality actually demand of you? Pick the answer closest to your view, and read its note.

d52c3881.text: Dawn. The queasiness is fading, and three lessons linger.

e2d68b11.text: From Epicurus: pleasure is the good, but tranquility and friends beat fleeting indulgence.

66434b18.text: From Bentham: aim for the greatest happiness for the greatest number. Sharing really was the better math.
